summary.description: PBDEs are thick liquids or solids used as flame retardants. They are non-flammable, non-volatile, and insoluble in water. PBDEs are known for their persistence in the environment and their tendency to bioaccumulate.
emission_sources: Disposal of PBDE-containing products in landfills or incinerators
Slow release from consumer products containing PBDEs
environmental_impact: Toxic to aquatic animals and long-term effects on aquatic environments
High levels of exposure may affect the brain and liver in humans

top_sdg_impacts.SDG12_Responsible_Consumption_and_Produc: PBDEs are released from poorly managed waste streams and consumer products, highlighting the need for safer chemical use and improved end-of-life disposal practices.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG14_Life_Below_Water: PBDEs are toxic to aquatic life, accumulate in the food chain, and cause long-term harm to marine ecosystems.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG3_Good_Health_and_Wellbeing: High exposure to PBDEs can damage human organs such as the brain and liver, raising concerns about their health effects, especially from long-term or occupational exposure.
